extracted.intended_audience: Voters/citizens and delegates considering the ratification and design of the national Constitution (People of the State of New York)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and prescribing the structural features, powers, checks, and selection procedures of a republican national Executive (President and Vice‑President) to maximize energy and prevent abuse. Covers election mechanics, term/duration, powers (military, treaties, appointments, pardons), and safeguards (responsibility, dependence on the people, plurality vs unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of office‑holders from electors
rubrics_metrics.description: No senator, representative, or other person holding a place of trust or profit under the United States, can be of the numbers of the electors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents immediate agents in the election from having a sinister bias; ensures electors are not persons whose present official interests would corrupt or mislead them. The transient and dispersed character of electors makes large‑scale corruption difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral College composition and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The people of each State shall choose a number of persons as electors equal to the number of senators and representatives of such State, who assemble within the State and vote for President; the person with a majority of the whole number of votes is President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmits votes to the seat of national government; majority required to be conclusive. If no majority occurs, the House selects from the five highest vote‑getters — a contingency procedure intended to ensure a decisive and qualified outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election process produces nationally credible candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of election affords a moral certainty that the office of President will never fall to any man who is not in an eminent degree endowed with the requisite qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talents that win in a single State by intrigue are unlikely to secure a sufficiently broad national consensus; the federal scale favors candidates of greater ability and virtue, producing a high probability of pre‑eminent characters filling the station.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive independence in continuance of office
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive should be independent for his continuance in office on all but the people themselves; re‑election should depend on a special body delegated to that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents temptation to sacrifice duty to those whose favor is necessary for duration of official consequence; making re‑election depend on a special electoral body secures independence from legislative or factional pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited fixed term and re‑eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The magistrate is to be elected for four years and is to be re‑eligible as often as the people think him worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fixed, limited term distinguishes the office from hereditary monarchy and balances permanence (duration as ingredient of energy) with opportunity for accountability and renewal; the text argues four years is less dangerous in the federal context than shorter terms in a single State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal accountability and impeachable responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is liable to be impeached, tried, and, upon conviction of treason, bribery, or other high crimes and misdemeanors, removed from office; and afterwards liable to prosecution and punishment in the ordinary course of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal responsibility (censure and punishment) is essential to republican safety; the President is not immune as a monarch is — this ensures public and legal remedies for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified veto with legislative override
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may return a bill passed by the two branches for reconsideration; the bill so returned becomes law if, upon reconsideration, it is approved by two‑thirds of both houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A qualified negative differs from the British absolute negative; it provides executive check while preserving legislative supremacy when strongly concurred upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander‑in‑chief with limited war prerogatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is commander‑in‑chief of the army and navy and of the militia when called into actual service, but declaration of war and the raising and regulating of fleets and armies belong to the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between supreme command/direction (executive function) and the sovereign prerogatives of declaring war and organizing forces (legislative functions); constrains executive military power to prevent monarchical prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pardoning power limited by impeachment exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The President has power to grant reprieves and pardons for offenses against the United States, except in cases of impeachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits executive clemency so it cannot nullify the constitutional impeachment process; contrasted with broader gubernatorial pardons in some States which might shelter preliminary conspiracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited convening and adjournment authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The President may recommend measures to Congress, convene both houses or either on extraordinary occasions, and in case of disagreement between them with respect to time of adjournment, adjourn them to such time as he thinks proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Executive practical ability to call and manage legislative sessions in exigent circumstances, but does not grant prorogation/dissolution powers analogous to a monarch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty‑making subject to Senate concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: The President has power, with the advice and consent of the Senate, to make treaties, provided two‑thirds of the senators present concur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents the President from being sole representative in binding foreign compacts; requires legislative branch participation to constrain executive foreign policy prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments by nomination with Senate advice and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The President nominates, and with the advice and consent of the Senate appoints, ambassadors, public ministers, Supreme Court judges, and other officers established by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public nomination and larger confirming body (Senate) reduce susceptibility to private influence and corruption compared with small secretive appointment councils; if Senate is divided, appointment cannot be made, providing a check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of the Executive as essential to energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is conducive to energy: decision, activity, secrecy, and despatch will generally characterize the proceedings of one man more than those of a greater number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single magistrate provides decisive, rapid action especially in emergencies (war, defense of laws and property); plurality dilutes these qualities and is therefore to be avoided for executive authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredients of executive energy
rubrics_metrics.description: The ingredients which constitute energy in the Executive are: first, unity; secondly, duration; thirdly, an adequate provision for its support; fourthly, competent powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers should combine these elements to produce an energetic Executive while balancing them with republican safeguards; each ingredient contributes to effective administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredients of republican safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The ingredients which constitute safety in the republican sense are: first, a due dependence on the people; secondly, a due responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive design must ensure the office remains responsive and accountable to the electorate; these safety ingredients are the countervailing principles to the energy ingredients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality or executive council undermines responsibility and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Plurality in the Executive (either many magistrates of equal dignity or one ostensible Executive subject to counselors) tends to conceal faults, destroy responsibility, produce dissension, and enervate administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plurality increases danger of personal emulation, faction, mutual recrimination (making it hard to assign blame), delays measures, and weakens execution especially in crises; councils may enable artful cabals or mutual shifting of blame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vice‑President election and independence of Senate representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Vice‑President is to be chosen in the same manner as the President, with the Senate exercising the selection role analogous to the House in Presidential contingency; selecting a senator as Vice‑President would exchange a constant for a contingent vote for the senator's State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids removing a sitting senator (a constant vote for a State) and thereby weakening that State's representation; the mode of selecting the Vice‑President should mirror safeguards used for the President because the VP may exercise supreme executive authority.
